title: Constructible fibre-dimension levels over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $h:Y\to T$ be a morphism of finite presentation: it is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], the inverse image of every affine open is quasi-compact, and its diagonal $Y\to Y\times_TY$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. For $t\in T$ let $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For every integer $n\geq0$, the subset $E_n=\{t\in T:\dim |Y_t|=n\}$ is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset], where dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. No smoothness, flatness, separatedness, or properness of $h$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05F9, lemma-dimension-fibres-constructible: locally constructible level sets for a finite-presentation morphism; on a Noetherian base these are constructible by a finite affine cover. Only the finite nonnegative levels are asserted here.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$. Local Noetherianity gives an affine cover of $T$ by spectra of Noetherian rings; quasi-compactness selects a finite subcover. Finite presentation implies finite type: the affine presentations have finitely many algebra generators and $h$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to $h$ to obtain $d\geq0$ with $\dim Y_t\leq d$ for every $t$. Thus every nonempty fibre has dimension a finite nonnegative integer.

source.place: Tag 05F9, lemma-dimension-fibres-constructible, second proof paragraph: Noetherian case; boundedness made explicit using morphisms.tex Tag 0A3V.

proof.text: Let $Z\subseteq|T|$ be any nonempty irreducible closed subset. Give it its reduced induced closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and choose its generic point $\xi$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. The projection $h_Z:Y\times_TZ\to Z$ is finitely presented by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], hence finite type. For $z\in Z$, its residue field in $Z$ equals its residue field in $T$: locally $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $z$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$, so both residue fields are $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$. Associativity from the fibre-product universal property therefore identifies $(Y\times_TZ)_z$ with $Y_z$. In particular their dimensions agree, including the empty case.

source.place: Tag 05F9, second proof paragraph: irreducible closed subscheme and its generic point; fibre identification expanded from the definitions.

proof.text: If $Y_\xi=\varnothing$, apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-avoidance] to $h$, $y=\xi$ and the closed subset $C=Y$. It gives an ambient open $V\subseteq T$ containing $\xi$ such that $h^{-1}(V\cap\overline{\{\xi\}})=\varnothing$. Since $\overline{\{\xi\}}=Z$, the nonempty relatively open $W=V\cap Z$ has only empty fibres. Their dimensions are $-\infty\ne n$, so $W\cap E_n=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 05F9, second proof paragraph: generic constancy, empty-fibre case supplied by Tag 054W, lemma-empty-generic-fibre.

proof.text: Otherwise Step 1 gives $\dim Y_\xi=m$ for some integer $m\geq0$. Apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-dimension-neighborhood] to the finite-type morphism $h_Z$ and generic point $\xi$. There is a nonempty open $W\subseteq Z$ on which every fibre has dimension $m$. By Step 2 these are the original fibres $Y_z$. If $m=n$, then $W\subseteq E_n$; if $m\ne n$, then $W\cap E_n=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 05F9, second proof paragraph: apply Tag 05F7, lemma-dimension-in-neighbourhood.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 provide the required nonempty relatively open subset for every irreducible closed $Z\subseteq|T|$. The finite affine Noetherian cover from Step 1 supplies the base hypothesis of [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion]. Apply that criterion to $E_n\subseteq|T|$ to conclude that $E_n$ is constructible. This applies to every $n\geq0$; if $T$ is empty the criterion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 05F9, second proof paragraph: Topology Tag 053Z, lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian.
